extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and communications/copywriters who write press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing the press release subheadline (deck/dek): a one-sentence summary under the headline that provides context, adds new information, and bridges to the lead paragraph. Focuses on format, style, content, and common pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / Function
rubrics_metrics.description: The deck provides additional context and supports the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides additional context; reinforces main message; encourages people to keep reading; bridges headline and lead paragraph; gives reader reason to continue; summarizes who/what/why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and concision (word count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the deck concise — ideally no more than 14 words; some sources allow up to 25 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One sentence maximum. Concise but informative. 'Every word counts.' Avoid being too long or losing impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-sentence maximum
rubrics_metrics.description: The deck should be a single sentence only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple sentences are a common mistake. The deck must remain a one-sentence summary that bridges to the first paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence case
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sentence case for the deck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use all caps. Sentence case improves readability and aligns with style expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the deck in active voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active constructions are clearer and more engaging than passive alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add new information (do not rephrase headline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The deck must add new information rather than simply rephrasing the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include who/what/why details not present in the headline; the deck should bridge to the first paragraph and provide a reason to continue reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include specifics (numbers, names)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, include concrete specifics such as numbers and names to make the deck informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: deployment metrics, percentage improvements, number of customers/companies, product names. Specifics increase credibility and newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridge to the lead paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: The deck should function as a bridge between the headline and the lead paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It should connect the hook of the headline with the first paragraph's details, preparing the reader to continue into the body copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standalone meaningfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: The deck should be meaningful on its own and work without the headline when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While it supports the headline, the deck should still convey a clear, standalone point or summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid clichés, buzzwords, and marketing-speak
rubrics_metrics.description: The deck should avoid vague, generic, or clichéd language and overt marketing jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No clichés, marketing-speak, or buzzwords. Be specific and factual rather than promotional-sounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common mistakes to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent errors that reduce deck effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not repeat the headline; avoid being too long; avoid vagueness or generic phrasing; avoid marketing-speak; avoid ALL CAPS; avoid multiple sentences. These weaken impact and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit subhead checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise checklist derived from the page's implicit rubric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 14–25 word limit; adds NEW information; includes specifics (numbers, names); sentence case; active voice; no buzzwords; bridges to first paragraph; standalone meaningful (works without headline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example of strong headline + deck combination
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative example showing how headline and deck should complement each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HEADLINE: "Acme Corp Unveils AI Platform That Cuts Document Processing Time by 75%" — DECK: "New Acme Intelligence reduces enterprise document review from hours to minutes, deployed at 50 Fortune 500 companies". Use concrete metrics/names and new detail in the deck.
